{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>MUTUAL CONFIDENTIALITY AND NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT</SPAN 0>
<SPAN 1>This Mutual Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure Agreement (“Confidentiality Agreement”) is made between Conference of State Bank Supervisors, Inc. (“Company”), and its affiliates and subsidiaries, whose principal offices are located at 1129 20th Street NW, Washington D.C. 20036 and <Vendor Name Here> whose principal offices are located at </SPAN 1><SPAN 2>_________________________________ </SPAN 2><SPAN 3>________________________________________________________________________________.</SPAN 3>
<SPAN 4>In consideration of each party’s provision of access to certain confidential information by the other in order to permit the parties to discuss current and future potential business relationships and perform their obligations under a Professional Services Agreement or other agreements or projects between Company and <Vendor Name Here> (collectively, “Project”) and for other good and valuable consideration, the sufficiency of which is acknowledged, it is agreed as follows:</SPAN 4>
<SPAN 5>1. Each party may be provided with access to selected information (oral, written, or electronic) of the other which helps meet a regulatory purpose or business need, including, but not limited to, that information which relates or refers to: business planning; internal controls; computer, data processing, or communications architectures or systems; electronic data processing architectures, applications, programs, routines, or subroutines; business affairs and methods of operation or proposed methods of operations, techniques or systems of a party or any customer of a party, financial or other non-public information, including but not limited to proposals, processes, forecasts, ideas, concepts, projections, analyses, software, hardware, marketing information, documentation, structure and protocols. </SPAN 5><SPAN 6>Some of the information in each of these categories is confidential in nature or constitutes a trade secret as it is not generally known to its competitors or the public. </SPAN 6><SPAN 7>This information received from a party, either orally or in writing, during the course of the Project shall be deemed to be confidential information (“Confidential Information”) for purposes of this Confidentiality Agreement. </SPAN 7><SPAN 8>Notes, documents, summaries or reports which are prepared from Confidential Information to the extent such specifically refer or relate to Confidential Information are themselves Confidential Information.</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>2. Each party acknowledges the sensitive and secret nature of the Confidential Information it will have access to during the term of the Project and agrees that it will treat such Confidential Information as strictly confidential and shall exercise the same degree of care in the protection of the Confidential Information as the receiving party exercises with respect to its own proprietary property and trade secrets, but in no event shall it be less than a reasonable degree of care given the nature of the Confidential Information.</SPAN 9>
<SPAN 10>3. Neither party shall disclose the Confidential Information received from the other to any person or entity, except its employees, officers, directors, independent consultants, affiliates, subsidiaries and other agents (collectively “Representatives”) involved in the performance of the Project, or to use the Confidential Information for any purpose other than fulfilling its obligations under the Project. </SPAN 10><SPAN 11>Each party acknowledges and agrees that breach of this Confidentiality Agreement by the other and/or anyone employed by or otherwise associated with the other may also constitute a violation of applicable laws. </SPAN 11><SPAN 12>Access to Confidential Information by the receiving party shall be limited to those Representatives who have agreed to be bound in writing under terms no less stringent than this Confidentiality Agreement.</SPAN 12>
<SPAN 13>4. Neither party shall make copies of the Confidential Information except for those copies required for use by Authorized Persons in the performance of the Project. </SPAN 13><SPAN 14>Each copy, including its storage media, shall be marked Confidential, and also include all copyright, trademark and other proprietary notices which appear on the original. </SPAN 14><SPAN 15>Each party agrees that all Confidential Information of the other party, including any copies thereof, shall be returned to the disclosing party upon request or destroyed within ten (10) business days of the expiration or other termination of the Project. </SPAN 15><SPAN 16>However, notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, </SPAN 16><SPAN 17>1) neither party will be required to delete electronic Confidential Information stored in back-up/archival storage in accordance with its policies, provided that any such retained Confidential Information will continue to be subject to the terms of this Confidentiality Agreement until it is destroyed by the receiving party; and </SPAN 17><SPAN 18>2) a single copy of all Confidential Information may be retained by the Receiving Party’s legal department for dispute resolution purposes only, provided, however, that such Confidential Information shall remain subject to the terms and conditions of this Confidentiality Agreement. </SPAN 18><SPAN 19>In the event that a receiving party has or acquires actual knowledge of any breach of the confidentiality of, or the misappropriation of, any Confidential Information received under this Confidentiality Agreement, such party shall promptly give notice thereof to the other party.</SPAN 19>
<SPAN 20>5. Upon written demand by the disclosing party or upon termination of this Confidentiality Agreement, the receiving party shall: </SPAN 20><SPAN 21>(i) cease using the Confidential Information, </SPAN 21><SPAN 22>(ii) return the Confidential Information and all copies, notes or extracts thereof to the disclosing party within ten (10) business days of receipt of demand; and </SPAN 22><SPAN 23>(iii) upon request of the disclosing party, certify in writing that the receiving party has complied with the obligations set forth in this paragraph. </SPAN 23><SPAN 24>Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, </SPAN 24><SPAN 25>1) neither party will be required to delete electronic Confidential Information stored in back-up/archival storage in accordance with its policies, provided that any such retained Confidential Information will continue to be subject to the terms of this Confidentiality Agreement until it is destroyed by the receiving party; and </SPAN 25><SPAN 26>2) a single copy of all Confidential Information may be retained by the Receiving Party’s legal department for dispute resolution purposes only, provided, however, that such Confidential Information shall remain subject to the terms and conditions of this Confidentiality Agreement.</SPAN 26>
<SPAN 27>6. All intellectual property rights associated with the Confidential Information, including without limitation, patent, trademark, copyright, trade secret rights, and moral rights shall remain in the disclosing party. </SPAN 27><SPAN 28>Moreover, this Confidentiality Agreement does not grant any right or license to a party, by implication or otherwise, to any intellectual property owned or controlled by the other party.</SPAN 28>
<SPAN 29>7. The obligation of non-disclosure shall not extend to: </SPAN 29><SPAN 30>(1) information which is then already in the possession of the receiving party and not under a duty of non-disclosure; </SPAN 30><SPAN 31>(2) information which is generally known or revealed to the public; </SPAN 31><SPAN 32>(3) information which is revealed to the receiving party by a third party, unless such party is under a duty of non-disclosure; </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>(4) information which the receiving party develops independently of the disclosure and such independent development can be shown by documentary evidence maintained contemporaneously with such development; or </SPAN 33><SPAN 34>(5) information that is disclosed with the disclosing party’s prior written consent.</SPAN 34>
<SPAN 35>8. In the event that a party receives a subpoena or other validly issued administrative or judicial process requesting Confidential Information received from the other, the receiving party shall provide prompt actual notice to, in the case of <Vendor Name Here>, the General Counsel of <Vendor Name Here>, and, in the case of Company, to the General Counsel of Company, of such receipt, providing the party with a reasonable opportunity to intervene in the proceeding before the time that the other party is required to comply with such subpoena or other process. </SPAN 35><SPAN 36>If such protective order or other remedy is not obtained, or the disclosing party waives compliance with the provision of this Confidentiality Agreement, the receiving party shall furnish only that portion of the Confidential Information which the receiving party is legally required to disclose and shall exercise its reasonable efforts to obtain reliable assurance that confidential treatment shall be accorded the Confidential Information. </SPAN 36><SPAN 37>Notwithstanding anything otherwise set forth herein, </SPAN 37><SPAN 38><Vendor Name Here> or Company may disclose Confidential Information: </SPAN 38><SPAN 39>a) to the extent revealed to a government agency with regulatory or oversight jurisdiction over Company; or </SPAN 39><SPAN 40>b) in the course of fulfilling any of <Vendor Name Here> regulatory responsibilities, including responsibilities under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Act) or other applicable law. </SPAN 40><SPAN 41>In either case, <Vendor Name Here> or Company shall furnish only that portion of the Confidential Information which the receiving party is legally required to disclose and shall exercise its reasonable efforts to obtain reliable assurance that confidential treatment shall be accorded the Confidential Information.</SPAN 41>
<SPAN 42>9. Each party acknowledges that the other, because of the nature of the Confidential Information, would suffer irreparable harm in the event of a material breach of the provisions of this Confidentiality Agreement in that monetary damages would be inadequate to compensate for such a breach, and that in the event of any material breach or threatened material breach by a party receiving Confidential Information from the other party of any such provisions, a party shall be entitled, in addition to such other legal or equitable remedies which might be available, to injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction against the threatened material breach or continuation of any such material breach without showing or proving any actual damages sustained by it. </SPAN 42><SPAN 43>Moreover, any such award of relief to the discloser of such Confidential Information shall include recovery of all actual and reasonable costs associated with enforcement of this Agreement including, without limitation, attorneys’ fees.</SPAN 43>
<SPAN 44>10. The Effective Date of this Confidentiality Agreement shall be the date it is signed by both parties and it shall terminate upon the earlier of </SPAN 44><SPAN 45>(i) thirty (30) days written notice of either party, or </SPAN 45><SPAN 46>(ii) three (3) years after the effective date.</SPAN 46>
<SPAN 47>11. The representations and obligations of each party relative to the Confidential Information shall survive the expiration or termination of this Confidentiality Agreement for a period of the longer of three (3) years or for such time as such Confidential Information remains a protectable trade secret under applicable law.</SPAN 47>
<SPAN 48>12. The rights and obligations of the parties hereunder are in addition to, and not in derogation of, their respective rights and duties under the Uniform Trade Secrets Act (“UTSA”) as adopted in the state set forth below or in respective state’s trade secrets laws, if UTSA has not been adopted.</SPAN 48>
<SPAN 49>13. This Confidentiality </SPAN 49><SPAN 50>Agreement contains the full and complete understanding of Company and <Vendor Name Here> with respect to the subject matter and supersedes all prior representations and understandings whether they be oral or written.</SPAN 50>
<SPAN 51>14. Company and <Vendor Name Here> understand and agree that in the event any part, term or provision of this Confidentiality Agreement is held to be invalid or legally unenforceable, the validity of the remaining parts, terms or provisions shall not be affected, and the rights and obligations of the parties shall be construed and enforced as if the Confidentiality Agreement did not contain the particular part, term, or provision held to be invalid. </SPAN 51><SPAN 52>This Confidentiality Agreement and performance thereunder shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York, excluding its conflicts of laws rules.</SPAN 52>
<SPAN 53>15. The parties acknowledge that the Confidential Information disclosed by each of them under this Confidentiality Agreement may be subject to export controls under the laws of the United States. </SPAN 53><SPAN 54>Each party shall comply with such laws and agrees not to knowingly export, re-export or transfer Confidential Information of the other party without first obtaining all required United States authorizations or licenses.</SPAN 54>
<SPAN 55>16. Neither party may assign this Confidentiality Agreement without the prior written consent of the other party. </SPAN 55><SPAN 56>However, either party may assign or transfer this Confidentiality Agreement and its rights hereunder to an affiliate or successor to its assets or liabilities if such assignee agrees in writing to be bound by the terms and conditions hereof and the non-assignment party is given notice of such an assignment. </SPAN 56><SPAN 57>Any assignment to the contrary shall be void.</SPAN 57>
<SPAN 58>17. The persons executing this Confidentiality Agreement warrant that they have the authority to bind <Vendor Name Here> and Company to the terms and conditions embodied in this Confidentiality Agreement.</SPAN 58>
<SPAN 59>18. Neither party makes or intends to make any warranty or representation of any kind concerning the Confidential Information, except each party represents and warrants that it has the right to disclose Confidential Information to Receiving Party. </SPAN 59><SPAN 60>Confidential Information is provided only for discussion purposes, is provided on an “As Is” basis, and Receiving Party relies on Confidential Information at its own risk.</SPAN 60>
<SPAN 61>19. As used in this Confidentiality Agreement, the terms “<Vendor Name Here>” and Company shall include any of their respective corporate affiliates or subsidiaries, provided that <Vendor Name Here> and Company </SPAN 61><SPAN 62>(a) shall be responsible for the observance and proper performance by all of their respective corporate affiliates of the terms and conditions of this Confidentiality Agreement, and </SPAN 62><SPAN 63>(b) if requested by the disclosing party, shall cause such corporate affiliate to return or destroy all Confidential Information in accordance with Section 5, prior to a corporate affiliate ceasing to be an affiliate thereof.</SPAN 63>
<SPAN 64>20. Independent Development: This Confidentiality </SPAN 64><SPAN 65>Agreement shall not be construed to limit the Receiving Party’s, or any of its Representatives’, right to independently develop or acquire products, services, or technology without use of the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information. </SPAN 65><SPAN 66>The Disclosing Party understands and acknowledges that the Receiving Party and/or its Representatives may currently or in the future be developing information, knowledge or technology internally, or obtaining information, knowledge or technology from other persons that may be similar to information, knowledge or technology contained or reflected in the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information.</SPAN 66>
<SPAN 67>21. Agreed and Accepted:</SPAN 67>

guidance.when: Assessing whether return or destruction is required upon termination of the agreement.
guidance.inspection: Identify both the required act and its triggering event. A duty triggered only by the discloser's request does not establish a termination-triggered duty; termination, expiration, rejection, conclusion, or abandonment must itself activate the duty.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative return-or-destruction duty together with language linking it to termination or an equivalent end event.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exception to a return or destruction obligation.
guidance.inspection: Check whether the exception expressly permits continued possession of backups, archival material, a legal copy, or another defined subset after the return/destruction event. Conditions on access, purpose, or continuing confidentiality do not negate the permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention exception and, when separated, the governing return/destruction clause showing the temporal context.

guidance.when: The agreement requires return or destruction of confidential information and copies without stating a retention exception.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether the duty is exhaustive as to the covered material and copies. A complete return/destruction command that leaves no authorized retained subset negates permission to possess some material afterward.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the exhaustive operative duty and verify across the complete agreement that no backup, archival, legal-copy, or other retention exception qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses ownership, licenses, or rights in confidential information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Look for language that no license or right is granted, conveyed, conferred, or implied. A limited authorization to review or use information for the stated transaction does not by itself contradict the broader no-grant proposition.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the express no-grant clause; include an ownership clause only when it helps establish the object of the denied rights.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts disclosure of negotiations, discussions, a contemplated transaction, or the existence of dealings between the parties.
guidance.inspection: Treat a prohibition on revealing that negotiations or discussions are occurring as covering the fact of the agreement or negotiation, even when the restriction is framed as disclosure to the public or media rather than as secrecy of the document itself.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the prohibition and the text identifying the protected fact; retain any governing introduction needed to show that the listed fact is prohibited from disclosure.

guidance.when: Confidential-information coverage is conditioned on marking, designation, or identification by the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that every covered disclosure mode is subject to an express identification mechanism, including any oral or non-written mode. A universal marking rule may use different procedures for written and oral disclosures.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite all clauses needed to cover each disclosure mode and its identification requirement; do not rely on one mode while another remains unconditional.

guidance.when: The definition covers information either expressly designated confidential or reasonably understood to be confidential from its nature or disclosure circumstances.
guidance.inspection: The contextual alternative independently covers undesignated information, so express identification by the disclosing party is not required for all confidential information.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete alternative definition showing both designation and circumstance- or nature-based coverage.

guidance.when: Assessing whether the receiving party may make any copy in some circumstance.
guidance.inspection: Find an express copying route, such as prior written consent, copies needed for authorized persons, or automatic backup creation acknowledged by the agreement. Permission may be conditional and need not be general.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite language expressly addressing copying, reproduction, or backup creation and the condition that authorizes it; access or disclosure permission alone is insufficient.

guidance.when: The agreement expressly prohibits copying confidential information.
guidance.inspection: If copying is barred and the complete agreement provides no condition under which the receiving party may copy, the conditional-copy permission hypothesis is negated. A consent exception would instead be a permission circumstance.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the copy prohibition and verify that no consent, operational-copy, backup, or other copying exception appears elsewhere.

guidance.when: The agreement permits disclosure to representatives or other persons.
guidance.inspection: Resolve who falls within the permitted class. Consultants, agents, counsel, accountants, professional advisers, affiliates, and similar non-employees establish sharing with some third parties; an employee-only exception does not.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the permission and the definition or enumeration proving that at least one permitted recipient is a third party, plus any need-to-know or confidentiality condition governing the permission.

guidance.when: The agreement states an authorized transaction, project, evaluation, business relationship, or other defined purpose for confidential information.
guidance.inspection: A command to use confidential information only for that purpose, or not for any other purpose, directly imposes the limited-use obligation. The existence of the authorized purpose is not a contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative use restriction and enough purpose language to identify the authorized scope.

guidance.when: Relevant candidate text is a numbered item, exception, continuation, anaphoric clause, or otherwise incomplete fragment.
guidance.inspection: Read the governing introduction and adjacent items to determine the item's legal function, trigger, subject, and exceptions. Keep independent operative clauses separately; do not treat a neighboring item as evidence merely because it shares the list.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include every span necessary to make the relied-on proposition complete, while excluding sibling items that do not establish that proposition.
